captions.text: Recap of chapter 05: a virtual environment keeps each project's packages separate.
pytest runs all your tests with one command.
HTTP is how programs talk, and Ollama is a small web server.
You've finished the primer. Now your code will talk to an AI.
Today's black box: how your code talks to a model.
Let's open it.
A model call is an HTTP request, just like the ones in chapter 05.
The body holds the model, the conversation and your settings.
requests.post sends it to Ollama. raise_for_status stops if something failed.
The reply text is inside the JSON, at message, then content.
You send a list of messages. Each message has a role. This one is from the user.
And here's the model's reply. Your code just talked to an AI.
A system message sets the rules for the conversation. It comes from you, the developer.
Same question, new rules. Clear, specific instructions work best.
To continue a conversation, you send all of it, including the model's earlier reply.
The word it only makes sense because the earlier messages are included.
Long replies take time. Streaming sends the reply piece by piece.
Ollama sends one line of JSON for each piece. A generator yields them.
Here we collect the pieces, then print the first six.
Each piece is a small chunk of text. Joined together, they make the reply.
Now, two puzzles. Predict the answers before the output appears.
Puzzle 1: ask for a cat name three times. Will the answers match?
Puzzle 2: tell it your name, then ask in a second call. Will it remember?
Three different answers, and it forgot the name. Why? The next chapter explains.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and build the pieces of a model call.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
